title: Ezekiel Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto me
I have set thee for a sign
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto me
questions.explanation: This statement appears first in Ezekiel 12:1, marking the beginning of the chapter.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the house of Israel in Ezekiel 12:2?
options: They will listen to the prophet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:2 states that the house of Israel is described as a 'rebellious house'.

questions.question: What are the people described as having in Ezekiel 12:2?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:2 mentions that they have 'eyes to see, and see not'.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel need to prepare according to Ezekiel 12:3?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:3 instructs him to prepare 'stuff for removing'.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 12:4, what should Ezekiel do with his stuff?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:4 commands him to bring forth his stuff by day in their sight.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel do in Ezekiel 12:5?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:5 instructs him to 'Dig thou through the wall in their sight'.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel carry his belongings in Ezekiel 12:6?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:6 states that he shall bear it upon his shoulders.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel do at evening according to Ezekiel 12:7?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:7 describes him bringing forth his stuff by day and carrying it in the evening.

questions.question: What happens in the morning in Ezekiel 12:8?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:8 states that the word of the LORD came unto him in the morning.

questions.question: What question do the people ask Ezekiel in Ezekiel 12:9?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:9 mentions that the house of Israel asked him, 'What doest thou?'.

questions.question: What burden does Ezekiel mention in Ezekiel 12:10?
options: The burden concerning the prince in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The burden concerning the prince in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:10 refers to a burden that concerns the prince in Jerusalem.

questions.question: The house of Israel is described as what in Ezekiel 12:2?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:2 describes the house of Israel as a 'rebellious house'.

questions.question: Ezekiel is instructed to carry his belongings in the twilight according to Ezekiel 12:6?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:6 states he shall carry it forth in the twilight.

questions.question: Ezekiel was told to ignore the people according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Ezekiel being instructed to ignore the people.

questions.question: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel every morning according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text only specifies that the word of the LORD came in the morning on one occasion, not every morning.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 12:12, what action does the prince among the people take during the twilight?
options: He bears upon his shoulder and digs through the wall carrying out thereby
He openly leads a rebellion against Babylon
He gathers the people for a feast
He prays to the LORD for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: He bears upon his shoulder and digs through the wall carrying out thereby
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:12 states, 'And the prince that is among them shall bear upon his shoulder in the twilight, and shall go forth: they shall dig through the wall to carry out thereby: he shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eyes.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 12:13 promise will happen if the prince digs through the wall and covers his face as commanded in Ezekiel 12:12?
options: He will be taken in God's snare and brought to Babylon, though he will not see it
He will successfully escape and live in peace
He will be honored as a hero among his people
He will find hidden treasure beyond the wall
questions.correctAnswer: He will be taken in God's snare and brought to Babylon, though he will not see it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:13 says, 'My net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare: and I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there,' which is the consequence of the action in verse 12.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 12:15, what will the people know when God scatters them among the nations?
options: That Babylon is their home now
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:15 states, 'And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall scatter them among the nations, and disperse them in the countries,' indicating the purpose of their scattering.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 12:14 and Ezekiel 12:15 connect in describing God's judgment?
options: Verse 14 describes the scattering and sword, and verse 15 highlights the knowledge gained of the LORD through this scattering
Verse 14 predicts peace, verse 15 promises victory
Verse 14 speaks of harvest, verse 15 of celebration
Verse 14 warns of famine, verse 15 about healing
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 14 describes the scattering and sword, and verse 15 highlights the knowledge gained of the LORD through this scattering
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:14 says God will scatter them and draw the sword after them, while 12:15 explains this will cause them to know He is the LORD, showing cause and effect.

questions.question: What is the purpose of God leaving a few men from the sword, famine, and pestilence as stated in Ezekiel 12:16?
options: So they may declare their abominations among the heathen and know that He is the LORD
To rebuild the temple in Jerusalem
To lead a rebellion against Babylon
To live in peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: So they may declare their abominations among the heathen and know that He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:16 explains that a few will be left to declare their abominations among the nations, making them aware of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 12:11, what is Ezekiel told to say about himself?
options: I am your sign; like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them
I am a prophet of peace and hope
I am a warrior for Israel's freedom
I am a servant of the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: I am your sign; like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:11 says, 'Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them,' indicating Ezekiel’s symbolic role.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 12:18 instruct the son of man to do with his bread and water?
options: Eat with quaking and drink with trembling and carefulness
Eat and drink joyfully with the people
Share with the poor and needy
questions.correctAnswer: Eat with quaking and drink with trembling and carefulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:18 commands, 'eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness,' reflecting the fearful times.

questions.question: Why will the land be desolate according to Ezekiel 12:19?
options: Because of the violence of all that dwell therein
Because the people fled to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the violence of all that dwell therein
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:19 states the land will be desolate 'because of the violence of all them that dwell therein,' linking judgment to their actions.

questions.question: What is the significance of covering the face in Ezekiel 12:12 when the prince goes out?
options: So he sees not the ground with his eyes
To hide his identity from the people
To protect himself from the sun
questions.correctAnswer: So he sees not the ground with his eyes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:12 says the prince 'shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eyes,' symbolizing shame or fear during captivity.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 12:20, what will happen to the cities that are inhabited?
options: They shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate
They shall be fortified and protected
They shall be given to the Babylonians peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:20 declares that the inhabited cities 'shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate,' as part of God's judgment.

questions.question: What attitude are the people of the land expected to have when they eat and drink according to Ezekiel 12:19?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:19 says they 'shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment,' showing fear due to the desolation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 12:14 say about those who try to help the prince?
options: They will be scattered toward every wind and the sword will follow them
They will be protected by God
They will lead the people back to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They will be scattered toward every wind and the sword will follow them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:14 states, 'I will scatter toward every wind all that are about him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the sword after them,' showing punishment for supporters.

questions.question: What does the LORD command Ezekiel to do in Ezekiel 12:11?
options: Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them
Lead a rebellion against the princes
questions.correctAnswer: Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:11 commands Ezekiel to say, 'I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them,' indicating his prophetic role as a living symbol.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 12:16 says that God will leave a few men alive so that they may declare their abominations among the heathen and know that He is the LORD.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:16 clearly states God will leave a few from the sword, famine, and pestilence so they may declare their abominations among the heathen and know that He is the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 12:19 promises that the land will prosper and be filled with abundance because of the violence of its inhabitants.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:19 says the land will be desolate because of the violence of the inhabitants, not prosperous.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 12.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will make cease in Ezekiel 12:23?
questions.explanation: The LORD states He will make the proverb cease, as noted in Ezekiel 12:23.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare about His words in Ezekiel 12:25?
questions.explanation: The LORD emphasizes that the word He speaks shall come to pass in Ezekiel 12:25.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 12:24, what will no longer exist within the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: The verse states that there will be no more vain vision or flattering divination in Israel as per Ezekiel 12:24.

questions.question: What do the people of Israel say about the visions in Ezekiel 12:27?
options: They are for many days to come
questions.correctAnswer: They are for many days to come
questions.explanation: The people claim that the vision is for many days to come in Ezekiel 12:27.

questions.question: What will happen to the proverb mentioned in Ezekiel 12:22?
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will make the proverb cease in Ezekiel 12:23.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 12:28, what does the LORD say about His words?
questions.explanation: The LORD states that none of His words will be prolonged and will be done as spoken in Ezekiel 12:28.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'מָשָׁל' (mashal) in Ezekiel 12:22 mean?
questions.explanation: 'מָשָׁל' (mashal) means 'proverb' as used in Ezekiel 12:22.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ezekiel 12:24 with the phrase 'vain vision'?
questions.explanation: The term 'vain vision' serves as a metaphor for false prophecies as seen in Ezekiel 12:24.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of prophecy in Ezekiel 12:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 55:11 connects as it emphasizes that God's word will accomplish what He desires, paralleling Ezekiel 12:25.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of rebellion found in Ezekiel 12:2?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:4 speaks of a rebellious nation, echoing the rebellious house theme in Ezekiel 12:2.

questions.question: What comes before Ezekiel 12:23?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:22 precedes Ezekiel 12:23, where the proverb is mentioned.

questions.question: What comes after Ezekiel 12:25?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:26 follows Ezekiel 12:25, continuing the message from the LORD.

questions.question: Ezekiel 12:4 includes a command to dig through what?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 12:4, the command is to dig through the wall, which signifies their upcoming captivity.

questions.question: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel multiple times in this chapter. True or False?
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel multiple times as seen throughout Ezekiel 12.

questions.question: Ezekiel was commanded to eat bread with quaking. True or False?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to eat bread with quaking in Ezekiel 12:18, not as a general command.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 12:2 teach about human sin?
options: Human rebellion leads to spiritual blindness and deafness
Human sin is easily forgiven without repentance
Humans are inherently unable to perceive God's word
Sin does not affect human perception of divine truth
questions.correctAnswer: Human rebellion leads to spiritual blindness and deafness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:2 describes the rebellious house as having eyes to see but not seeing, and ears to hear but not hearing, illustrating the doctrine that sin causes spiritual insensitivity and rebellion against God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 12:11 teach about God's judgment and prophetic signs?
options: God uses prophetic actions as signs to confirm His judgments
Prophetic signs are symbolic only and lack fulfillment
God's judgments are arbitrary and lack warning
God's signs are hidden and not meant for public understanding
questions.correctAnswer: God uses prophetic actions as signs to confirm His judgments
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:11 states that Ezekiel himself is a sign and that as he acted, so shall it be done to the people, confirming that God uses prophetic signs to communicate and validate His coming judgments.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty is taught in Ezekiel 12:25?
options: God's word will come to pass without delay according to His sovereign will
God's promises are often delayed and uncertain
Human free will can thwart God's decrees
God's word depends on human actions for fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: God's word will come to pass without delay according to His sovereign will
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:25 emphasizes that God will speak and perform His word promptly, demonstrating His sovereign control over the fulfillment of prophecy and history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 12:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:13 shows God's sovereignty in capturing the prince and bringing him to Babylon, orchestrating events according to His divine plan.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 12:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:24 declares that there will be no more vain visions or flattering divinations, affirming God's faithfulness to speak true words that come to pass.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 12:15 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's judgment on nations?
options: It shows God dispersing Israel among nations to manifest His judgment
It denies that God judges nations and only judges individuals
It emphasizes Israel's ultimate victory without judgment
It portrays judgment as temporary and superficial
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God dispersing Israel among nations to manifest His judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:15 speaks of God scattering Israel among the nations as a judgment, which aligns with the biblical theme of God judging nations through exile and dispersion.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 12:18 foreshadow the experience of exile as portrayed elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It metaphorically depicts the anxiety and fear during exile
It promises immediate restoration without suffering
It denies that exile will affect daily life
It treats exile as a brief and insignificant event
questions.correctAnswer: It metaphorically depicts the anxiety and fear during exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:18 commands eating and drinking with trembling and carefulness, foreshadowing the fearful and anxious experience of exile seen throughout the Old Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 12:22 and Ezekiel 12:23 teach about prophecy and God's timing?
options: God's word will no longer be delayed but fulfilled promptly
Prophecies are always distant and impossible to confirm
Human skepticism about prophecy proves its falsehood
Visions are meaningless and should be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: God's word will no longer be delayed but fulfilled promptly
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:22 and 12:23 address the proverb that visions are delayed, declaring that God will end such delays and bring His word to fulfillment in due time.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 12:4 and Ezekiel 12:12 teach about God's judgment on leadership?
options: Leaders will experience exile as a sign of God's judgment
Leaders are exempt from divine judgment and exile
God punishes only the people, sparing the prince
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders will experience exile as a sign of God's judgment
questions.explanation: Both verses describe the prince bearing his burden and going into captivity, revealing that God’s judgment includes leaders being taken into exile.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 12:14 and Ezekiel 12:16 teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God judges by scattering but preserves a remnant for witness
God shows mercy by ignoring sin completely
God's justice is indiscriminate and without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God judges by scattering but preserves a remnant for witness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:14 describes scattering and sword after them, but 12:16 promises a few survivors to declare abominations among the nations, showing both judgment and mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 12:26-28 teaches that prophetic visions are always far off and irrelevant for the current generation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God's words will no longer be prolonged; prophecies will be fulfilled in the current generation
Prophecies are always distant and have no relevance today
Visions are symbolic and do not predict actual events
Prophecies depend on human interpretation and may never happen
questions.correctAnswer: God's words will no longer be prolonged; prophecies will be fulfilled in the current generation
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:26-28 rebukes the idea that visions are for distant times, affirming that God's word will be fulfilled promptly in the days of the rebellious house.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 12:19 teach regarding the consequences of sin upon the land?
options: Sin leads to desolation and fear in the land's inhabitants
Sin has no impact on the physical land
The land is inherently cursed without human sin
God blesses the land regardless of human behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to desolation and fear in the land's inhabitants
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:19 describes eating and drinking with carefulness and astonishment because the land is desolate due to the inhabitants' violence, teaching the doctrine of sin's effect on the land.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 12:25 specifically reveal about God's nature in relation to prophecy?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:25 states that God will speak and perform His word without delay, highlighting His faithfulness and reliability in prophecy fulfillment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 12:7 contribute to the narrative arc of prophetic enactments in Scripture?
options: It models the use of symbolic actions to communicate divine judgment
It discourages prophets from using physical signs
It emphasizes silent prophecy without public demonstration
It denies the importance of prophecy in Israel's history
questions.correctAnswer: It models the use of symbolic actions to communicate divine judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:7 recounts Ezekiel carrying out the commanded sign act, illustrating the biblical motif of prophets using enacted signs to reveal God's message.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 12:1 and Ezekiel 12:9 teach about prophetic communication and the people's response?
options: God commands prophets to deliver messages even to rebellious, questioning people
Prophets should only speak to willing listeners
God's word is always accepted without doubt
Prophetic messages are private and not meant for public scrutiny
questions.correctAnswer: God commands prophets to deliver messages even to rebellious, questioning people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 12:1 and 12:9 show God instructing Ezekiel to prophesy despite the people's rebellious questions, affirming the doctrine of faithful prophetic proclamation.
